# Separating Non-Algal Particles (NAP) from Bulk TSS {#nap}

```{r ch3-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
```

Our additive Beer–Lambert model partitions non-water light attenuation among three mutually exclusive pools: phytoplankton (`Chl a`), non-algal suspended particles (`NAP`: mineral sediment and detritus), and dissolved organic matter (`DOC`). Because standard gravimetric filtration measures bulk **Total Suspended Solids (`TSS`)**—which captures both mineral sediment and living algal cells on the filter—we subtract living phytoplankton dry mass from bulk `TSS` before fitting the model:

| Optical Component | Field Measurement | Model Predictor & Units |
|---|---|---|
| Phytoplankton ($\alpha_{\text{Chl }a}\,\text{Chl }a$) | Chlorophyll *a* ($\mu\text{g L}^{-1}$) | $\text{Chl }a$ ($\text{mg m}^{-3} = \mu\text{g L}^{-1}$) used directly |
| Non-algal particles ($\alpha_{\text{NAP}}\,\text{NAP}$) | Bulk TSS / SSC ($\text{mg L}^{-1}$) | $\text{NAP} = \text{TSS} - \text{biomass}(\text{Chl }a)$ ($\text{mg L}^{-1}$) |
| Dissolved organic matter ($\alpha_{\text{DOC}}\,\text{DOC}$) | DOC ($\text{mg L}^{-1}$) | $\text{DOC}$ ($\text{mg L}^{-1}$) used directly |

Following Gohin et al. (2005), we estimate phytoplankton dry biomass ($\text{mg L}^{-1}$) from $\text{Chl }a$ ($\mu\text{g L}^{-1}$) as a power law that accounts for intracellular photoacclimation (lower carbon-to-chlorophyll ratios in nutrient-rich blooms; Geider et al. 1997; Cloern et al. 1995):

$$\text{biomass}_{\text{algal}}\ [\text{mg L}^{-1}] = 0.234\,(\text{Chl }a)^{0.57}, \qquad \text{NAP} = \text{TSS} - 0.234\,(\text{Chl }a)^{0.57}$$

```{r nap-fig, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.3, fig.cap = '(a) Empirical TSS vs. Chl a across matchups overlaid with the nonlinear Gohin et al. (2005) algal biomass curve (solid black) and constant linear dry-mass:Chl a ratios (dashed). Constant 100:1 or 200:1 lines cut above measured TSS during high-chlorophyll blooms, producing unphysical negative NAP. (b) Distribution of the non-algal fraction of bulk suspended solids (NAP / TSS) by water-body type.'}
tr <- get_training()
set.seed(42)
tr_sub <- tr %>% slice_sample(n = 15000)
chl_grid <- tibble(chl_a = 10^seq(-1, 3, length.out = 200)) %>%
  mutate(
    `Gohin et al. (2005): 0.234 × Chl^0.57` = 0.234 * chl_a^0.57,
    `Linear 100:1 (0.10 × Chl)` = 0.100 * chl_a,
    `Linear 200:1 (0.20 × Chl)` = 0.200 * chl_a
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(-chl_a, names_to = 'curve', values_to = 'biomass')

p_a <- ggplot(tr_sub, aes(chl_a, tss)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = type), alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(data = chl_grid, aes(chl_a, biomass, linetype = curve), colour = 'black', linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number()) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1000), labels = scales::label_number()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = TYPE_COLS) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted'), name = 'Algal Biomass Model') +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom', legend.direction = 'vertical', panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = expression(Chlorophyll~italic(a)~(mu*g~L^-1)),
       y = expression(Bulk~TSS~(mg~L^-1)),
       title = '(a) Bulk TSS vs. Algal Dry-Biomass Curves')

p_b <- tr %>%
  mutate(nap_frac = pmin(1, pmax(0, tss_dead / tss))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(nap_frac, fill = type, colour = type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = TYPE_COLS, name = 'Water-body type') +
  scale_colour_manual(values = TYPE_COLS, name = 'Water-body type') +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom', panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = 'Non-Algal Particle Share of Bulk TSS (NAP / TSS)',
       y = 'Density',
       title = '(b) Non-Algal Share of Suspended Solids')

p_a + p_b
```

## Sensitivity to Biomass Formulation & Method Tiers

Comparing the Gohin et al. (2005) power law against constant linear dry-mass:Chl *a* ratios (`50:1`, `100:1`, `200:1`) shows that constant high ratios over-predict algal mass in blooms (generating up to **31.7%** negative NAP), whereas the power law produces negative NAP in only **2.02%** of samples while yielding virtually identical attenuation slopes:

```{r ratio-sens, echo = FALSE}
ratios <- tibble(a = P$chl_ratio_sensitivity)
neg <- ratios %>% mutate(res = map(a, ~ add_nap(get_simul('no_secchi'), a = .x) %>%
                                     summarize(pct_negative_nap = mean(tss_dead < 0) * 100))) %>%
  unnest(res)
k_w <- get_k_w()
slopes <- ratios %>% mutate(fit = map(a, function(a) {
  d <- add_nap(tr %>% select(-chl_ratio, -power, -chl_a_biomass, -tss_dead), a = a)
  m <- lm((kd - k_w) ~ 0 + tss_dead + doc + chl_a, data = d)
  tibble(NAP = coef(m)[1], DOC = coef(m)[2], Chl_a = coef(m)[3],
         R2 = cor(d$kd, fitted(m))^2)
})) %>% unnest(fit)
left_join(neg, slopes, by = 'a') %>%
  mutate(form = ifelse(a == 234, '0.234 × Chl^0.57 (Gohin et al. 2005; canonical)',
                       paste0(a / 1000, ' × Chl (constant linear ', a, ':1)'))) %>%
  select(form, pct_negative_nap, NAP, DOC, Chl_a, R2) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, col.names = c('Algal Dry-Biomass Formulation (mg/L)', '% Samples with NAP < 0', 'α_NAP (m²/g)', 'α_DOC (m²/g)', 'α_Chl a (m²/mg)', 'Global R²')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```

Similarly, restricting calibration strictly to top-tier analytical methods (`Tier 1` chemistry and `Tier 1–2` Secchi) yields nearly identical attenuation slopes while pooling all harmonized AquaMatch tiers nearly triples spatial coverage:

```{r tier-qa, echo = FALSE}
tr_strict <- tr %>% filter(chl_tier == 1, doc_tier == 1, tss_tier == 1, sdd_tier <= 2)
m_all    <- coef(lm((kd - k_w) ~ 0 + tss_dead + doc + chl_a, data = tr))
m_strict <- coef(lm((kd - k_w) ~ 0 + tss_dead + doc + chl_a, data = tr_strict))
tibble(
  Subset = c('All harmonized AquaMatch tiers (canonical training set)',
             'Strict top analytical tiers only (Tier 1 chemistry, Tier 1–2 Secchi)'),
  `Observations (n)` = fmt_n(c(nrow(tr), nrow(tr_strict))),
  `Unique Sites` = fmt_n(c(n_distinct(tr$SiteID), n_distinct(tr_strict$SiteID))),
  `α_NAP (m²/g)` = c(m_all[1], m_strict[1]),
  `α_DOC (m²/g)` = c(m_all[2], m_strict[2]),
  `α_Chl a (m²/mg)` = c(m_all[3], m_strict[3])
) %>% kable(digits = 4) %>% kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```
